title: Sprint Baton and Regional Handoff Playbook for Runtime/Console/API Launches
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Goal: produce a concise, operational playbook that sequences sprint-level 'baton' handoffs between runtime, console, and API owners across regional launch windows. This ticket covers: 1) a canonical handoff checklist (who does what when), 2) defined readiness gates per lane (runtime, console, API), 3) emergency rollback signals and contact flow, and 4) capacity hedging and surge lanes for regional staggered launches. This playbook is intended to reduce cross-team ambiguity during week-of-launch and improve time-to-detect / time-to-remediate for regressions that span multiple surfaces.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Playbook reviewed and acknowledged by runtime, console, API, and SRE leads.
2) Three staged checklists (preflight, go-window, post-rollout) published in Confluence and linked from Launch Calendar.
3) On-call runbook entries created for top-3 cross-surface incidents with clear owner and rollback step.
4) Capacity hedging thresholds and surge activation doc validated against last-quarter traffic traces.
5) Playbook dry-run completed during Release Rehearsal (notes captured).

notes: Trade-offs discussed: tight preflight windows reduce blast radius but increase ops overhead; we prioritized predictable small windows with automated rollbacks. Decision: default to 30-minute preflight window + automated gating; can widen per-project based on risk profile. Also discussed the use of shadow warmup vs traffic mirroring and chose shadow for privacy and cost controls.
